experiments.title: A measured joule becomes warm water
experiments.script:
# A measured joule becomes warm water
# Expectation: 10 kJ into 100 g water should raise temperature roughly 24 K, without mass loss below boiling.
register lv3
add v1 water 100g
heat v1 10kJ
inspect v1
measure v1 thermometer
measure v1 balance
experiments.expected_result: 10 kJ into 100 g water should raise temperature roughly 24 K, without mass loss below boiling.
experiments.observed_result: 48.9117 C and 100.0000 g after the pulse; temperature rose 23.9117 K.

experiments.title: Undo a thermal pulse
experiments.script:
# Undo a thermal pulse
# Expectation: Heating then removing the same 10 kJ should return 100 g water close to its initial temperature and mass.
register lv3
add v1 water 100g
heat v1 10kJ
cool v1 10kJ
inspect v1
experiments.expected_result: Heating then removing the same 10 kJ should return 100 g water close to its initial temperature and mass.
experiments.observed_result: Returned to 25.0000 C with the original water inventory.

experiments.title: Mix unequal hot and cold portions
experiments.script:
# Mix unequal hot and cold portions
# Expectation: 75 g at 20 C plus 25 g at 80 C should equilibrate near 35 C; mass should be 100 g.
register lv3
add v1 water 75g @ 20C
add v1 water 25g @ 80C
inspect v1
experiments.expected_result: 75 g at 20 C plus 25 g at 80 C should equilibrate near 35 C; mass should be 100 g.
experiments.observed_result: 35.0000 C and 100 g, matching the weighted mean.

experiments.title: A double dose is not a double temperature rise
experiments.script:
# A double dose is not a double temperature rise
# Expectation: Equal 10 kJ pulses into 100 g and 200 g water should produce approximately 2:1 temperature rises.
register lv3
add v1 water 100g
new
add v2 water 200g
heat v1 10kJ
heat v2 10kJ
inspect
experiments.expected_result: Equal 10 kJ pulses into 100 g and 200 g water should produce approximately 2:1 temperature rises.
experiments.observed_result: Temperature rises were 23.9117 K and 11.9559 K, giving a 2.000 ratio.

experiments.title: Latent heat intercepts the cooling pulse
experiments.script:
# Latent heat intercepts the cooling pulse
# Expectation: Removing 20 kJ from 100 g water initially at 5 C should give an ice/water mixture near 0 C, not liquid at -43 C.
register lv3
add v1 water 100g @ 5C
cool v1 20kJ
inspect v1
measure v1 ph
experiments.expected_result: Removing 20 kJ from 100 g water initially at 5 C should give an ice/water mixture near 0 C, not liquid at -43 C.
experiments.observed_result: Ice and liquid coexist at approximately 0 C. Aqueous pH is explicitly withdrawn.

experiments.title: Boiling spends energy on disappearing liquid
experiments.script:
# Boiling spends energy on disappearing liquid
# Expectation: 40 kJ into 100 g water at 95 C should approach 100 C and evaporate roughly 17 g rather than heat all liquid to 190 C.
register lv3
add v1 water 100g @ 95C
heat v1 40kJ
inspect v1
measure v1 ph
experiments.expected_result: 40 kJ into 100 g water at 95 C should approach 100 C and evaporate roughly 17 g rather than heat all liquid to 190 C.
experiments.observed_result: 100 C plateau with 83.2 g remaining, approximately 16.8 g evaporated. Settled pH is withdrawn.

experiments.title: Heat dilution cannot invent energy
experiments.script:
# Heat dilution cannot invent energy
# Expectation: Mixing two equal water portions at 60 C should keep them near 60 C, not reset the second dose to room temperature.
register lv3
add v1 water 50g @ 60C
add v1 water 50g @ 60C
inspect v1
experiments.expected_result: Mixing two equal water portions at 60 C should keep them near 60 C, not reset the second dose to room temperature.
experiments.observed_result: 60.0000 C after both additions, with 100 g water.

experiments.title: A tenfold acid dilution
experiments.script:
# A tenfold acid dilution
# Expectation: Diluting 0.001 mol HCl in 100 mL water with another 900 mL should raise pH by about one unit (roughly 2 to 3).
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 HCl 0.001mol
measure v1 ph
dilute v1 900mL
measure v1 ph
inspect v1
experiments.expected_result: Diluting 0.001 mol HCl in 100 mL water with another 900 mL should raise pH by about one unit (roughly 2 to 3).
experiments.observed_result: pH changed from 2.0381 to 3.0135, a rise of 0.9754.

experiments.title: Acid/base cancellation and overshoot
experiments.script:
# Acid/base cancellation and overshoot
# Expectation: 0.001 mol HCl followed by equal NaOH should reach near-neutral pH; another 0.001 mol NaOH should make it alkaline.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 HCl 0.001mol
add v1 NaOH 0.001mol
measure v1 ph
add v1 NaOH 0.001mol
measure v1 ph
inspect v1
experiments.expected_result: 0.001 mol HCl followed by equal NaOH should reach near-neutral pH; another 0.001 mol NaOH should make it alkaline.
experiments.observed_result: Equal acid/base doses gave pH 6.9927; excess base gave 11.9275.

experiments.title: Weak acid versus strong acid
experiments.script:
# Weak acid versus strong acid
# Expectation: Equal 0.001 mol doses in 100 mL should give acetic acid a higher pH than HCl, by at least one unit.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 HCl 0.001mol
new
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 CH3COOH 0.001mol
measure v1 ph
measure v2 ph
inspect
experiments.expected_result: Equal 0.001 mol doses in 100 mL should give acetic acid a higher pH than HCl, by at least one unit.
experiments.observed_result: HCl pH 2.0381 versus acetic acid 3.3871, a difference of 1.3490.

experiments.title: Half-neutralisation exposes a pKa
experiments.script:
# Half-neutralisation exposes a pKa

register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 CH3COOH 0.01mol
add v1 NaOH 0.005mol
measure v1 ph
inspect v1
experiments.expected_result: 0.01 mol acetic acid and 0.005 mol NaOH in 100 mL should form a buffer around pH 4.5-5.0.
experiments.observed_result: pH 4.6630, within the frozen expected interval.

experiments.title: A buffer survives a small acid pulse
experiments.script:
# A buffer survives a small acid pulse

register lv3

add v1 NaOH 0.005mol
measure v1 ph
new
add v2 water 100mL
measure v2 ph
add v1 HCl 0.0001mol
add v2 HCl 0.0001mol
measure v1 ph
measure v2 ph
experiments.expected_result: A half-neutralised acetate buffer should change pH far less than plain water after the same 0.0001 mol HCl pulse.
experiments.observed_result: Buffer pH changed by 0.0173; water changed by 3.9839 under the same acid pulse.

experiments.title: Neutral salt is an ionic conductor
experiments.script:

register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
measure v1 conductivity

measure v1 conductivity

experiments.expected_result: Adding 0.001 mol NaCl to 100 mL water should increase conductivity substantially while leaving pH approximately neutral.
experiments.observed_result: Conductivity rose from 0.0551 to 1204.2742 microS/cm; pH remained 6.9968.

experiments.title: Common ions make a silver cloud
experiments.script:
# Common ions make a silver cloud

add v1 NaCl 0.001mol
add v1 AgNO3 0.001mol
inspect v1
experiments.expected_result: 0.001 mol each of NaCl and AgNO3 in 100 mL should produce close to 0.001 mol solid AgCl, with conserved silver and chloride.
experiments.observed_result: Approximately 0.998 mmol AgCl formed from 1 mmol feeds.

experiments.title: Precipitation cannot depend on bottle order
experiments.script:
# Precipitation cannot depend on bottle order

add v1 AgNO3 0.001mol
new

inspect
experiments.expected_result: Reversing the equal silver/chloride additions should leave essentially equal AgCl solid amounts and pH in the two vessels.
experiments.observed_result: Both orders gave the same solid yield, pH, temperature, and final inventories within the checked tolerances.

experiments.title: Remove the cloud without removing the salt water

new

inspect

experiments.observed_result: Approximately 1 mmol AgCl remained in v1. Water and dissolved Na/Cl/nitrate transferred to v2.

experiments.title: Chalk dissolves in acid

experiments.title: Drying a dilute salt solution

evaporate v1 0.9
inspect v1
measure v1 balance
experiments.expected_result: Evaporating 90% of the solvent from 0.001 mol NaCl in 100 g water should conserve sodium/chloride while increasing concentration roughly tenfold.
experiments.observed_result: Water fell to 10 g while 1 mmol sodium/chloride remained. Vaporisation enthalpy is explicitly outside this operator's balance.

new

experiments.title: Splitting and reuniting a solution
experiments.script:

inspect v1
new
decant v1 v2 0.4
decant v2 v1 1
inspect
experiments.expected_result: Decant 0.4 into v2 then all of v2 back to v1 should restore initial inventory, temperature, and pH within numerical tolerance.
experiments.observed_result: The reunited contents and temperature match the initial solution; v2 was empty.

experiments.title: A small sealed headspace makes fizz push back
experiments.script:
# A small sealed headspace makes fizz push back

experiments.expected_result: The same acid/carbonate doses should produce higher final pressure over 10 mL than 100 mL sealed headspace.
experiments.observed_result: Pressures were 128.016 kPa for 10 mL and 114.854 kPa for 100 mL.

experiments.title: Uncorking releases the compressed gas
experiments.script:
# Uncorking releases the compressed gas

register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
seal v1 10mL
add v1 NaHCO3 0.001mol
add v1 HCl 0.002mol
open v1
measure v1 pressure
inspect v1

experiments.title: Fixed pressure trades pressure rise for expansion
experiments.script:

add v1 NaHCO3 0.001mol
add v1 HCl 0.002mol
measure v1 pressure
inspect v1
experiments.expected_result: Acid/carbonate under 1 bar regulation should stay near 1 bar and increase gas volume or explicitly state the unsupported constraint.

experiments.title: Sweeping carbon dioxide out
experiments.script:
# Sweeping carbon dioxide out
# Expectation: A nitrogen sweep after a finite CO2 dose should lower retained carbon and raise pH relative to the carbonated state, with a gas-transfer account.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
seal v1 100mL
add v1 CO2 0.001mol
measure v1 ph
sweep v1 1bar
wait 60s
measure v1 ph
inspect v1
experiments.expected_result: A nitrogen sweep after a finite CO2 dose should lower retained carbon and raise pH relative to the carbonated state, with a gas-transfer account.
experiments.observed_result: pH rose from 4.3475 to 6.9974 and represented carbon was removed with explicit outward gas events.

add v1 water 100mL
add v1 CuSO4 0.001mol
add v1 Zn 0.002mol

experiments.expected_result: Zinc in 0.001 mol CuSO4 solution should produce copper metal and consume zinc; mass/inventory should show the exchange.
experiments.observed_result: Approximately 0.99646 mmol copper plated while the same amount of zinc was consumed. Both metal totals were conserved.

experiments.title: Copper refuses the reverse displacement
